projectContext.description: voiceover-matcher-subtitle: AI-powered pipeline for matching voiceover to stock footage

userStories.title: Generate sprint stories for pipeline focus area
acceptanceCriteria: Read scripts/ralph/config/ralph-config.json to understand the 'pipeline' focus area
Read scripts/ralph/session/prompt.md for project context and architecture notes
Read scripts/ralph/state/queue.json for interview details (story outline, architecture decisions, key files)
Read CLAUDE.md for project conventions and known issues
Analyze the codebase to find 8-12 specific improvements for 'pipeline'
Add stories US-81-002 through US-81-012 to scripts/ralph/state/prd.json (MUST use sprint-prefixed IDs)
Each story MUST have 4-6 testable acceptance criteria
Each story MUST have a 'notes' field with: (1) tier classification, (2) exact source file paths, (3) line number ranges if removing/moving code
IMPORTANT: All generated stories MUST have passes set to false - do NOT run tests or evaluate whether they already pass
IMPORTANT: Story IDs MUST follow format US-81-NNN to be unique across sprints
Mark this story (US-81-001) as passes: true when done
userStories.notes: Seed story. Generated 11 pipeline-focused stories based on codebase analysis. Key findings: metadata extraction, chapter detection, title scoring, tag boost, and LLM context enrichment are ALL already implemented. Stories focus on actual pipeline gaps: per-item error isolation, partial stage resume, progress reporting, stage dependency declaration, data quality validation, and pipeline-level parallelism.

userStories.title: Add per-item error isolation to batch pipeline stages
acceptanceCriteria: CAPTION stage continues processing remaining videos when a single caption fetch fails, collecting errors in a per-video error dict
DOWNLOAD_SEGMENTS stage continues downloading remaining segments when one segment download fails, collecting errors per segment
Failed items are logged with structured error info (video_id, error_type, message) and included in StageResult.data['failed_items']
StageResult.metrics.items_failed count matches the actual number of failed items
A test verifies that when 1 of 5 items fails in a batch, the stage still returns success=True with 4 processed items and 1 failed item
userStories.notes: Tier: foundation. Added failed_items list to SegmentDownloadStats with video_id tracking in increment_failure(). CAPTION stage now builds failed_items from caption_results and returns StageMetrics with items_failed/items_processed. DOWNLOAD_SEGMENTS already had per-item error isolation; added failed_items to checkpoint_data. 7 tests cover both stages.

userStories.title: Add partial stage resume for long-running download stages
acceptanceCriteria: DOWNLOAD_SEGMENTS stage saves incremental progress to checkpoint after every N downloads (configurable, default 10)
When resuming a DOWNLOAD_SEGMENTS stage via --resume, already-downloaded segments are detected on disk and skipped
The incremental checkpoint includes a 'partial_progress' dict with keys: completed_ids, failed_ids, total_count
A test verifies that after interrupting at 5/20 downloads and resuming, only the remaining 15 are attempted
Checkpoint partial_progress is cleared when the stage completes fully
userStories.notes: HARD STORY: Skipped after 30_minute_limit - pending decomposition

userStories.title: Add centralized pipeline progress reporting with stage-level granularity
acceptanceCriteria: A new ProgressReporter class in src/pipeline_progress.py provides a unified progress interface
ProgressReporter tracks current_stage, items_total, items_completed, items_failed, elapsed_seconds, and estimated_remaining_seconds
Pipeline.run() passes ProgressReporter to each stage, and stages call reporter.update(completed=N) during batch processing
ProgressReporter writes a progress.json file to the project directory, updated at most every 5 seconds
A test verifies that ProgressReporter correctly computes ETA based on throughput (items_completed / elapsed_seconds * items_remaining)
userStories.notes: Implemented ProgressReporter in src/pipeline_progress.py with start_stage/update/finish_stage/finish_pipeline API. Pipeline.run() creates reporter, starts/finishes stages, and sets state._progress_reporter for stage access. DOWNLOAD_SEGMENTS and CAPTION stages call reporter.update() during batch processing. progress.json written with 5s throttle via atomic rename. 13 tests cover ETA computation, snapshots, file I/O, and pipeline lifecycle.

userStories.title: Add data quality gate between MATCH and OUTPUT stages
userStories.notes: All 5 criteria verified. Implementation in src/pipeline.py (_check_match_coverage_gate). Config in config.yaml (pipeline.quality_gates.min_match_coverage). 7 tests in tests/test_pipeline_quality_gate.py all pass: below-threshold warning, above-threshold no warning, exact threshold, custom threshold, zero segments, zero matches, info log.
acceptanceCriteria: After MATCH stage completes, a validation check verifies that at least 50% of voiceover segments have a match (configurable threshold)
If match coverage is below threshold, a warning is logged with specific guidance: 'Only N/M segments matched (X%). Consider running with --force-rematch or checking video search results.'
The quality gate threshold is configurable via config.yaml under pipeline.quality_gates.min_match_coverage (default 0.5)
The quality gate does NOT abort the pipeline - it logs a warning and continues (non-blocking by default)
A test verifies that the warning is emitted when match coverage is below threshold and NOT emitted when above

userStories.title: Add explicit stage dependency declarations to pipeline stages
acceptanceCriteria: Each stage class defines a DEPENDS_ON class attribute listing stage names it requires (e.g., MatchStage.DEPENDS_ON = ['ANALYZE', 'CAPTION'])
Each stage class defines a PRODUCES class attribute listing state attributes it outputs (e.g., CaptionStage.PRODUCES = ['caption_results', 'text_metadata'])
Pipeline.run() validates that all dependencies are satisfied before running each stage (dependency stages must be completed in checkpoint or current run)
A test verifies that running MATCH without CAPTION raises a clear DependencyError with message naming the missing dependency
A test verifies that the existing STAGE_ORDER is consistent with declared dependencies (no stage runs before its dependencies)
userStories.notes: Added DEPENDS_ON and PRODUCES class attrs to Stage base class (backward-compatible defaults). All 7 stages declare explicit dependencies. DependencyError class added. Pipeline.run() validates deps via _validate_stage_dependencies() tracking completed/restored stages. 21 tests in tests/test_stage_dependencies.py cover: declarations on all stages, STAGE_ORDER consistency, DependencyError on missing deps, dependency names in error messages, checkpoint restore counting.

userStories.title: Add throughput metrics tracking to batch pipeline stages
acceptanceCriteria: StageMetrics dataclass gains new fields: items_per_second (float), peak_items_per_second (float), and throughput_samples (list of float)
CAPTION, MATCH, and DOWNLOAD_SEGMENTS stages compute and report items_per_second in their StageResult.metrics
Throughput is computed using a sliding window (last 10 items) rather than overall average, giving more accurate recent throughput
Pipeline timing summary (_print_timing_summary) includes throughput column showing 'N items/sec' for batch stages
A test verifies that throughput metrics are correctly computed from a sequence of timed item completions
userStories.notes: Throughput metrics added to StageMetrics (items_per_second, peak_items_per_second, throughput_samples). CAPTION, MATCH, DOWNLOAD_SEGMENTS stages compute throughput via sliding window. Timing summary includes throughput column. 15 new tests pass.

userStories.title: Add pipeline dry-run validation that checks all stage inputs upfront
acceptanceCriteria: Pipeline.validate_all() runs validate_inputs() for ALL stages in order, collecting all validation errors before failing
When run with --dry-run flag, the pipeline calls validate_all() and reports which stages would run, which would skip, and which have validation issues
validate_all() checks config validity for each stage (e.g., embedding provider configured, cache dirs writable) without executing any stage
Output is a structured summary: stage name, status (skip/run/error), validation message
A test verifies that validate_all() catches a missing voiceover file and reports it for the ANALYZE stage without running any stage
userStories.notes: Added StageValidationResult dataclass and validate_all() public method to PipelineOrchestrator. validate_all() runs _validate_config() for pipeline-level checks (CONFIG entries) then iterates all stages calling validate_inputs(), collecting ALL errors without short-circuiting. Returns structured List[StageValidationResult] with stage_name/status/message. Refactored _run_dry_run to delegate to validate_all(). 15 tests in tests/test_pipeline_validate_all.py cover structured output, error collection, filters, config errors, no-execution, missing voiceover detection with real AnalyzeStage, and dry-run integration.

userStories.title: Add configurable failure threshold for batch stage abort decisions
acceptanceCriteria: New config option pipeline.batch_failure_threshold (float, default 0.5) controls when a batch stage aborts vs continues
When failure rate exceeds threshold during a batch stage, the stage aborts immediately with a clear error message listing all accumulated failures
When failure rate is below threshold, the stage continues processing remaining items and reports partial success
The threshold is checked after each batch item completes, not just at the end
A test verifies that with threshold=0.3, a batch of 10 items aborts after the 4th failure (3 fails + 1 success already = 75% fail rate > 30%)

userStories.title: Add pipeline stage timing predictions based on historical data
acceptanceCriteria: After each pipeline run, per-stage timing data (duration, items_processed, throughput) is appended to a pipeline_history.json file in the project directory
Before running a stage, pipeline logs an estimated duration based on average of last 3 runs for that stage with similar item counts
Estimation uses items_count from the current run and historical throughput to predict duration
If no history exists, no estimate is logged (graceful degradation)
A test verifies that with 3 historical runs averaging 10 items in 30 seconds, a new run with 20 items estimates ~60 seconds
userStories.notes: Tier: observability. Currently timing is only reported after completion. Predicting duration helps users plan. Source files: new src/pipeline_history.py (load/save history, compute estimates), src/pipeline.py (log estimates before stage, save timing after stage). Keep the history file small - only last 10 runs per stage. Use project dir so each project has its own history.

userStories.title: Add cross-stage data drift detection to pipeline orchestrator
acceptanceCriteria: After each stage completes, pipeline validates that output counts match expectations (e.g., caption_results count >= 80% of video_ids count)
Drift rules are defined as a list of (source_field, target_field, min_ratio) tuples in PipelineOrchestrator
When drift is detected, a warning is logged: 'Data drift: {target_field} has {actual} items but {source_field} has {expected} (ratio: {ratio:.1%}, threshold: {min_ratio:.0%})'
Drift detection does not abort the pipeline - it only warns (non-blocking)
A test verifies that drift warning is emitted when caption_results has 5 items but video_ids has 20 (25% ratio < 80% threshold)
userStories.notes: Tier: reliability. A partial data drift check exists for video_ids vs caption_results (US-44-010) but there's no systematic cross-stage validation. Source files: src/pipeline.py (add _check_data_drift after each stage, define drift rules as class constant). Drift rules: VIDEO_SEARCH->CAPTION (video_ids vs caption_results, 0.8), MATCH->OUTPUT (matches count vs voiceover_segments count, 0.5), CAPTION->MATCH (text_metadata vs video_ids, 0.8).

userStories.title: Add pipeline event hooks for extensible stage lifecycle callbacks
acceptanceCriteria: PipelineOrchestrator supports registering multiple callbacks for events: before_stage, after_stage, on_stage_error, on_pipeline_complete
Callbacks receive a PipelineEvent dataclass with fields: event_type, stage_name, timestamp, data (dict), error (optional)
Existing on_stage_start and on_stage_complete callbacks are migrated to use the new event system
Multiple callbacks can be registered per event type and are called in registration order
A test verifies that registering 2 callbacks for after_stage results in both being called with correct PipelineEvent data
userStories.notes: Tier: architecture. Currently pipeline has on_stage_start/on_stage_complete as single callbacks. A proper event system enables plugins (progress reporter, metrics exporter, logging hooks) without modifying pipeline code. Source files: src/pipeline.py (add PipelineEvent dataclass, event registry, register_hook/emit_event methods). Keep backward compatible - existing callback params still work.
